Follow-up to #86. While closing the three pm-evidence polynomial-ReDoS alerts, the fleet was scanned for the same regex shapes over agent-supplied text.

Findings outside this package (not fixed by #86's PR, per scope):

- `pm-todos/index.ts:185` — `HEADER_RE = /^(#{1,6})[ \t]+(\S.*)$/`. The title is one greedy pass with no lazy-quantifier tail, so it is linear today, but it is one edit away from the retired pm-evidence shape. Recommend the same linear-scanner treatment when next touched.
- `pm-changelog/src/check-drift.ts:29` and `:42`, and `pm-changelog/src/generator.ts:1647` — heading and closing-sequence alternations such as `(?:[-*_]\s*){3,}$` inside line classification. Each is analyzed linear on disjoint alphabets (the same false-positive class as pm-evidence alert #1), but CodeQL's polynomial model can flag them; they currently parse changelog and tracker prose that agents supply.

Suggested action in those packages: either restate the line classifiers as single-pass scanners (as pm-evidence now does) or add measured linearity tests plus a documented dismissal rationale, mirroring the pm-evidence pattern. No CodeQL alert is currently open on those repositories; this is preventive hardening, not an active defect.
Follow-up: harden sibling heading-regex shapes flagged by the same CodeQL polynomial model (pm-todos, pm-changelog)
